project: Restore Go Build-Cache Reuse in Git Worktrees
description: Stop forcing go build -a solely because a factory worker runs in a Git worktree. Recover and address the original staleness concern with the narrowest evidence-backed cache policy, prove that cross-worktree builds always reflect current source and preserve version behavior, and demonstrate a material warm-build speedup for make build and make install.

context.customerAsk: Remove the blanket go build -a behavior from Git worktrees and solve any original staleness risk precisely. Record the guard's history in the PR, prove that a main-checkout build followed by worktree builds and a worktree source modification never produces a stale binary, compare make build and make install with forced-rebuild equivalents, and publish before/after wall-time evidence. This lane owns only the WORKTREE_FLAGS block and build-cache flags in the root Makefile.
context.problem: The root Makefile compares git-common-dir with git-dir and sets WORKTREE_FLAGS to -a for every linked worktree. All factory lanes run in that topology, so make build, make install, verify-build, and default repeatedly rebuild the Go standard library and dependency graph instead of reusing valid content-addressed cache entries. Repository history shows the block first appearing in commit 826929a692b17490c922fec2fe05b4b9cd9fc35b with only a stale-cache comment and no recorded reproducer in the commit message, so the original correctness intent must be investigated and preserved through direct behavioral evidence.
context.solution: Use Go's content-addressed build cache by default in worktrees and remove unconditional -a. Complete the guard archaeology, reproduce a main-checkout/worktree/source-mutation scenario with an observable binary probe, and introduce narrower cache keying or isolation only if evidence identifies a real missing input such as environment, cgo, or VCS metadata. Prove build/install artifact and version parity against explicit forced-rebuild controls, then record comparable before, primed, and warm wall times in the PR.

acceptanceCriteria: The PR records the available history and rationale for the worktree guard, including commit 826929a692b17490c922fec2fe05b4b9cd9fc35b, any recovered original staleness scenario, and the evidence supporting the selected cache policy.

make build and make install no longer force go build -a solely because the checkout is a Git worktree; any replacement cache isolation or cache-key input is narrowly scoped to a reproduced correctness risk.

A clean main-checkout build, a linked-worktree build, and a rebuild after an observable source change in that worktree each produce the behavior expected from their own source, with no stale cross-worktree binary.

Cache-enabled make build and make install outputs are byte-identical to, or behaviorally equivalent to, comparable forced -a controls, including the same CLI version/VCS stamping and successful installed-binary behavior.

The PR records equivalent before/after worktree timing commands and environment assumptions; an immediate warm cache-enabled make build is materially faster than the forced-rebuild baseline, with the expected improvement from minutes toward seconds or any variance explained with evidence.

Scope remains limited to the root Makefile's worktree/build-cache flags and the smallest direct behavioral verification needed; lint-driver mechanics, cmd/unitlane, functional targets, public contracts, UI, generated artifacts, and unrelated cleanup remain unchanged.

Quality gates pass: focused cross-worktree build/install verification, relevant Go tests, and Typecheck pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, conflicts or adjacent Makefile churn are resolved against current origin/main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Preserve source freshness while enabling cached worktree builds
userStories.description: As an implementation worker building from a linked worktree, I want the build to reuse valid cached packages and still reflect my worktree's current source so that fast builds never execute stale code.
acceptanceCriteria: The PR archaeology identifies the guard's introducing commit and searches available commit, blame, PR, and issue context for the motivating staleness case; unsupported assumptions are explicitly labeled, and the chosen policy is tied to recovered or reproduced evidence.
Being in a Git worktree no longer adds -a to the ordinary make build or make install command.

If a cache-key risk is demonstrated, the implementation isolates only that risk through a documented deterministic input or cache boundary; if no risk is demonstrated, ordinary Go content-cache behavior remains the source of truth without new process-global or repository-local cache state.

In a controlled scenario, the main checkout builds a binary, a linked worktree builds its binary, an observable package or version-probe behavior is changed only in the worktree, and the next worktree build exhibits the changed behavior while the main-checkout result remains unchanged.

Reverting or changing the worktree probe again causes the next build to exhibit the new expected behavior, proving that both cache hits and invalidation are correct rather than passing from a one-time clean build.

The scenario is verified on the repository's supported CI platform and includes Windows-safe path handling where automation is added; it does not delete broad user cache directories or mutate a developer's installed binary as test setup.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed the available guard archaeology: 826929a692b17490c922fec2fe05b4b9cd9fc35b is the first available Makefile/blame point for the worktree block, and its associated PR #1359 changed only cron functional coverage; neither the commit message, associated PR discussion, nor available commit comments recovered a cache-staleness reproducer or issue. That unsupported historical intent is now documented explicitly. Removed the worktree-only -a policy from the root Makefile and replaced it with empty-by-default GO_BUILD_FLAGS, preserving make GO_BUILD_FLAGS=-a build/install as an explicit comparison control. On Windows with the shared Go cache, a main-checkout binary and linked-worktree binary both returned probe code 1; changing only cmd/factory/main.go in the worktree produced 37, then 73, and reverting produced 1 again, while the main artifact remained at 1. The final cache-enabled make build completed in 3.577 seconds to a temporary output path. Temporary source and artifacts were restored/isolated; no installed binary or broad cache directory was modified. make -n confirms no default -a in build/install and explicit -a remains available. make typecheck, make test, and focused cmd/factory/pkg/root tests pass. The initial clean-build wrapper attempt was terminated by concurrent host Go-build contention, so no unsupported cold-build timing claim is made here; warm timing belongs to story 002.

userStories.title: Prove build/install parity and warm-build throughput
userStories.description: As a factory operator repeating build and review cycles, I want cached worktree builds to preserve release-relevant output while completing dramatically faster so that throughput improves without changing the shipped CLI.
acceptanceCriteria: From equivalent source and environment inputs, cache-enabled and explicit forced -a make build controls are byte-identical, or a documented behavioral comparison proves equivalent CLI startup, --version output, VCS/dirty-state stamping, and representative command behavior.

make install uses the same corrected cache policy as make build; its installed binary passes the same version/behavior probe as the corresponding build artifact without overwriting an unrelated user installation during verification.

verify-build and default inherit the corrected build behavior through their existing dependency on build; no adjacent lint, unit-lane, functional-lane, or UI mechanics are changed to manufacture the timing result.

The PR includes before and after timing for make build in a fresh linked worktree under comparable Go version, source revision, host-load, and cache-state conditions, plus an immediate unchanged warm rerun.

The warm cache-enabled result is materially faster than the forced -a baseline and trends from minutes toward seconds; the PR reports raw wall times and explains material variance rather than claiming an unsupported percentage.
Focused build/install probes and the repository's required build-related CI checks pass with no version-stamping regression.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed parity and throughput verification on Windows 11-era host tooling with go1.25.0 windows/amd64, CGO_ENABLED=1, source revision 6c81ae487cad95487e9931139aa43bf7622aa5b2, and a fresh detached linked worktree. The sequential benchmark used an isolated temporary GOCACHE and shared GOMODCACHE, temporary BIN_DIR/INSTALL_DIR values, and isolated HOME/USERPROFILE; it never touched a user installation or deleted a broad cache. Exact commands were make BIN_DIR=.artifacts/worktree-build-cache-002/cache-build build, the same unchanged warm build, make INSTALL_DIR=.artifacts/worktree-build-cache-002/cache-install install, make GO_BUILD_FLAGS=-a BIN_DIR=.artifacts/worktree-build-cache-002/forced-build build, and make GO_BUILD_FLAGS=-a INSTALL_DIR=.artifacts/worktree-build-cache-002/forced-install install. Raw wall times were cold cache build 109.321s, unchanged warm cache build 3.346s, warm cache install 3.898s, forced build 25.536s, and forced install 30.937s; the warm cache build is materially faster than the explicit forced baseline on the same sequential host run, while the cold run explains the initial cache priming cost. All four artifacts had the identical SHA-256 6a4667af82485916ce1bbf82070133790d2998ad615f20e5669d6b3af9c716ab. All four build/install binaries returned identical --version output v0.0.8-0.20260810184644-947152348b23+dirty and identical --help output; go version -m reported identical vcs.revision 947152348b235f3dd0ede47f233947fcadddcc6a, vcs.time 2026-08-10T18:46:44Z, and vcs.modified=true for every artifact. The linked-worktree Go metadata reflects the common checkout's state (the main checkout had unrelated dirty files), but cached and forced controls are equivalent and -a does not correct that separate stamping behavior. make -n verify-build expanded to ui-build followed by make build and a cache-enabled go build; make -n default likewise emitted cache-enabled go build, while only explicit GO_BUILD_FLAGS=-a emitted -a. Focused cmd/factory and pkg/root tests, make test, make typecheck, make backend-size, make pkg-maint, make pkg-file-count, make pkg-structure, and make vet all passed. No adjacent lint, unit-lane, functional-lane, UI, generated, or public-contract mechanics changed.
